root.name: Latvian Gambit Accepted: Bilguer Variation
root.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 f5 3. Nxe5 Qf6 4. d4 d6 5. Nc4

overview: After 3.Nxe5 Qf6 4.d4 d6 5.Nc4 fxe4 Black has given a pawn for the White e-pawn, and 6.Nc3 Qg6 7.Ne3 is the typical continuation. Black aims at the open f-file and White's kingside with ...Nf6, ...Be7 and ...O-O, while White simply keeps the extra pawn and completes development. White should stand better with accurate play.

white_ideas.idea: Keep the extra pawn and drive Black's queen with Nc3 and Ne3
Develop Be2 or Bc4 and castle
Avoid early tricks on the f-file and h4-d8 diagonal

black_ideas.idea: Use the open f-file and ...Bc5 or ...Be7 for an attack
Look for tactics against a slow white king

typical_structures.structure: Open e- and f-files with White pawn on d4 and Black pawn on d6
White knights on c4 and e3, Black queen on g6 or f6

character.notes: Open and tactical, with Black taking risks to catch up in development.

gambit.notes: White wins the e5 pawn and can hold it.

soundness.notes: The Latvian is a dubious anchor; this main line leaves White a pawn up with a safe position.

structure.notes: e-pawn trades and the f-file open early.

character.reason: Tactical, open play with Black attacking down the f-file.

gambit.reason: Black plays 2...f5 and loses the e-pawn for activity.

soundness.reason: Latvian Gambit is a soundness anchor for dubious.

structure.reason: Central pawns come off and lines open.

approach.reason: Latvian Gambit is an offbeat anchor.

level.reason: Dubious, never Beginner; the tactics are not deep.

plans.reason: Black plays for development and an early queen on f6/g6.
